video_title: This Rune Giant Deck is TOTALLY OVERPOWERED!!

rune-giant: clock 2:36-2:02: refuses to open with her against a suspected Lava Hound deck — "I don't really want to Rune Giant first because it looks like he has Lava Hound, and I typically want to wait for them to go for their Lava Hound or just something in the back, and then I go in opposite lane" (303-313s), expanded at 324-338s: "just say I go Rune Giant to the back, he can just Lava into it ... but then that Rune Giant would just be completely wasted, so I do prefer to just like wait for them, get a little bit of tempo, and then I can just start attacking them".

clock 1:51: the only back-line Rune Giant of the game, at tile (9, 0), released once two conditions were met — "I think now I can go for the Rune Giant in the back because I do have the Evo E-Barbs and he doesn't have the Skelly Dragons in cycle either" (350-355s).

clock 0:58: played defensively at (8, 10) as a kiting body against a Valkyrie crossing, then followed with Mother Witch — "let's go for the Rune Giant here to kite this and then we can go for the Mother Witch as well" (402-405s).

clock 0:37 and OT 1:59: bridge Rune Giants at (3, 15) in the lane he is already grinding, gated on the opponent's building being out of cycle — "Let's Rune Giant the bridge again, though, cuz he has no Tombstone" (423-425s). Two mechanics notes: "I like how the Rune Giant doesn't move anymore when it's upgrading things. I feel like that was a pretty good change" (416-419s), and he tracks the enchant targets — "we didn't enchant the Hoggies. Not bad" (465s).
zap: clock 2:50: his stated default opener with this deck, Zap straight onto the enemy left tower at tile (3, 25) for 77 HP — "My favorite play with this deck is just zapping the tower first play. I feel like there's no risk to it, and you're also just getting to your Evo right away, which will help you kill combos, you know, like Archer Queen and stuff like that that you're not normally able to kill" (289-300s).

clock 1:55 and OT 1:51 / 1:27: three more tower Zaps at (14, 26), (2, 22) and (4, 23); in overtime the chip is the explicit win plan — "we just need two Zaps and a Fireball just to finish off this game. Let's Zap here as well. We need one more Zap and a Fireball, guys" (491-497s). The enemy left tower goes 400 -> 323 on the OT 1:27 Zap.
fireball: clock 2:22: added to a bridge Elite Barbarians push purely as an elixir drain, not for value — "I'm going to Fireball as well, to be honest. There's no point not to. I'm just going to force out a bunch of Elixir" (319-323s), label at (12, 15).

clock 1:07 and 0:50: two Fireballs at (3, 21) behind the left-lane Elite Barbarians push while the enemy left tower falls 4781 -> 2649 — "this is going to be some nice damage ... We forced out the Evo Zap and we can get two shots on the tower" (395-400s).

clock 0:14 and OT 1:37: used defensively on his own half, at (2, 10) into the Lava Hound push ("Okay, let's Fireball this", 447s, HUD-confirmed elixir -4) and at (3, 14) onto Skeleton Dragons as the first card of a pre-announced three-card defence ("Let's go for the Fireball here and then we can go for the Minions as well. And in case he has an Evo Zap, I need a Heal Spirit as well", 484-489s).
elite-barbarians: clock 2:25: evolved Elite Barbarians at the right-lane bridge tile (14, 15) with Heal Spirit attached one second later — "Let's just E-Barbs Heal Spirit here" (317s); enemy right tower 4858 -> 4583.

clock 1:10: the big push, released off a card-count read rather than an elixir lead — "Wait, hold on. He has no ground cards. Let's just E-Barbs at the bridge. He has the Skelly Dragons" (390-393s). The enemy left tower drops 4781 -> 3875 -> 3262 -> 2649 in the following four seconds.

clock 1:26: used as leverage while still in hand — he forces the opponent's Tombstone out with Mother Witch pressure specifically so it is unavailable later: "Forcing out the Tombstone is very good as well cuz if we can kill it, then he won't have the Tombstone for the E-Barbs" (372-377s).
OT 1:59: first card of the overtime counter-push at (3, 14), ahead of Rune Giant and Berserker into the same tile — "Okay, let's go for the Rune Giant. Let's go for the Berserker as well" (461-463s).
mother-witch: clock 1:57: pre-declared as the Tombstone answer and as a card that constrains the opponent's hand — "we do have the Mother Witch for the Tombstone, so he has to be making sure that he's saving either Fireball or like an air unit just to instantly block it every time" (341-348s).

clock 1:41-1:37: played at (8, 13)/(9, 13) as an information probe, expecting to lose the exchange — "if I Mother Witch like this, more often than not he'll just Mega Minion on top of it, which is fine by me. I just need to know what he's able to do. Let's go for the Mother Witch here. Force him to go for the Fireball and then we can go for the Minions" (358-367s). He then plans around the spell landing on her: "he has no Evo Zap, so he's not going to be able to take out our Minions as well after he fireballs the Mother Witch" (407-412s).

clock 0:28 and 0:08: used for the Cursed Hogs as blockers and as a counter-push under a Lava Hound attack — (8, 9) "Just keep this alive. Spawn a piggy to block. Perfect" (437-439s), then (8, 7) with the trade stated explicitly: "we just want to get the counter push off of the Mother Witch. Even though we are going to take some damage, I feel like getting this counter push is a little bit more important cuz we need to win the game right here, right now, or we are dead" (450-459s).

OT 1:44: (7, 10) to keep the pressure on in overtime — "let's Mother Witch here again. Just keep up the pressure here cuz he's going to have to watch out for these Piggies. He does a nice ability, which is fine by me. It's going to spawn a Piggy" (477-484s).
minions: clock 1:31, 0:50, 0:37, 0:08, OT 1:35, OT 1:17: always the announced follow-up behind another card, never the lead — "Force him to go for the Fireball and then we can go for the Minions" (365-367s) into (12, 15); "he has no Evo Zap, so he's not going to be able to take out our Minions as well after he fireballs the Mother Witch" (407-412s); "We can go for the Minions as well" (425s) into (1, 14); "Let's go for the Minions as well and then we can go for another Mother Witch" (448-450s) into (2, 11); "then we can go for the Minions as well" (486s) into (2, 13).

clock 0:08 - OT 1:35: doubles as the anti-air answer in the Lava Hound lane, placed at (2, 11) and (2, 13) with Fireball and Heal Spirit around them while the Lava Hound and Skeleton Dragons come down the left.
berserker: clock 2:45 and 1:17: 2-elixir back-line cycle placements at (3, 12) and (9, 0) after explicitly rejecting the bridge option — "Can I Berserker the bridge? Okay, I'll just Berserker in the back here. We have the Evo E-Barbs and we can go for a Rune Giant as well" (381-387s).

clock 0:47 and OT 1:59: bridge Berserkers at (3, 15) in the attacking lane, both times alongside a Rune Giant — "Okay, let's go for the Berserker at the bridge, too" (413-414s); "Let's go for the Berserker as well" (463s).

clock 0:19 and OT 1:19: defensive/cycle body at (1, 7) under the Lava Hound push and at (8, 10) in the closing overtime rotation — "I needed to go for the Berserker. Let's just do our quickest cycle possible" (501-503s). No hero ability is named anywhere in this game; he is played as the normal card.
heal-spirit: clock 2:25: attached directly behind the bridge Elite Barbarians at (14, 14), one second after them — "Let's just E-Barbs Heal Spirit here" (317s).

clock 0:19 and OT 1:33: played pre-emptively rather than reactively, ahead of expected burst damage — "We have to Heal Spirit preemptively cuz I feel like he's going to go for a ability" (443-446s) at (1, 6), and "in case he has an Evo Zap, I need a Heal Spirit as well. Just keep this alive" (487-490s) at (3, 12) behind Fireball and Minions.
tombstone: clock 2:36: the opponent's Tombstone at (8, 19) is the card that tells Ryley the whole deck — "Okay, he has a Tombstone" (302s), immediately followed by "it looks like he has Lava Hound" (305s).

clock 1:26-1:23: he values killing/forcing it by what it will not be available for — "Forcing out the Tombstone is very good as well cuz if if we can kill it, then he won't have the Tombstone for the E-Barbs" (372-377s), and later times a bridge Rune Giant to its absence: "Let's Rune Giant the bridge again, though, cuz he has no Tombstone" (423-425s). His stated answer to it is Mother Witch (341-348s).
lava-hound: clock 2:36-2:02: read from the Tombstone before it ever appears, and it dictates his opening — "it looks like he has Lava Hound, and I typically want to wait for them to go for their Lava Hound" (305-309s); a back-line tank into it is a wasted card, "he can just Lava into it, and then he can just easily like defend from there" (324-330s).

clock 0:28-0:03: the actual Lava Hound push arrives at (4, 13) with Balloon and pups and takes his left tower 4781 -> 2115; he answers with Berserker, Heal Spirit, Fireball, Minions and Mother Witch rather than a big body, having already noted the support was spent — "if he goes for the Lava, he has no support cards for it, only a Balloon" (432-435s).
skeleton-dragons: clock 2:18 onward: the opponent's Skeleton Dragons are his cycle clock for committing a Rune Giant — "he doesn't have the Skelly Dragons in cycle either" (353-355s) is one of the two conditions for the back-line Rune Giant at clock 1:51, and "He has the Skelly Dragons" (393s) is the caveat on the left-lane Elite Barbarians push.

clock 0:31 and OT 1:44-1:38: forcing them out is treated as stripping the Lava Hound of support — "He has to get Skelly Dragons down. That's good cuz now if he goes for the Lava, he has no support cards for it, only a Balloon" (430-435s); in overtime they come down his left lane and he answers with Fireball at (3, 14) plus Minions and Heal Spirit (484-490s).
mega-minion: clock 1:47-1:41: identified by playing a Mother Witch as bait and watching the answer — "Okay, he has Mega Minion, that's good to know. So, if I Mother Witch like this, more often than not he'll just Mega Minion on top of it, which is fine by me. I just need to know what he's able to do" (356-363s).
balloon: clock 0:27-0:03: named as the opponent's only remaining Lava Hound support once the Skeleton Dragons are spent — "if he goes for the Lava, he has no support cards for it, only a Balloon" (432-435s), then "He might go for a Balloon, though. We have to be careful" (439-442s); a Balloon is tracked at (5, 9) at t=454s during that push.
valkyrie: clock 1:07-1:02 and OT 1:19: the opponent's Valkyrie is tracked crossing at (13, 21) -> (14, 16) and later at (2, 13); Ryley answers the first one with a Rune Giant placed to kite plus Mother Witch behind it — "let's go for the Rune Giant here to kite this and then we can go for the Mother Witch as well" (402-405s). He never names the card on camera.
archer-queen: clock 2:47: mentioned only, not played by either side — cited as the sort of card the evolved Zap opener lets this deck finish: "you're also just getting to your Evo right away, which will help you kill combos, you know, like Archer Queen and stuff like that that you're not normally able to kill" (295-300s).

bullets: Game 3 of 8 in a single-deck Rune Giant showcase (video t=288.5-513.5), vs a Lava Hound / Tombstone / Skeleton Dragons beatdown. Result: win, in overtime — "Let's go. Very nice win and I will see you all in the next match" (507-509s).

The deck is piloted as bridge pressure, not beatdown: the only back-line Rune Giant of the game (clock 1:51) is gated on two explicit conditions ("I do have the Evo E-Barbs and he doesn't have the Skelly Dragons in cycle either", 350-355s), and every other win-condition placement is at or over the bridge — Elite Barbarians (14, 15) at clock 2:25, Elite Barbarians left lane at clock 1:10, Berserker (3, 15) at clock 0:47, Rune Giant (3, 15) at clock 0:37 and again at OT 1:59.

Against a Lava Hound deck he refuses to lead with the tank at all: "I don't really want to Rune Giant first because it looks like he has Lava Hound ... just say I go Rune Giant to the back, he can just Lava into it, and then he can just easily like defend from there ... so I do prefer to just like wait for them, get a little bit of tempo, and then I can just start attacking them" (303-338s).

Chip damage carries the deck as much as the pushes do. His stated first play every game is Zap on the tower ("My favorite play with this deck is just zapping the tower first play. I feel like there's no risk to it, and you're also just getting to your Evo right away", 289-296s), and in overtime the finish is counted out in spells: "we just need two Zaps and a Fireball just to finish off this game" (491-494s), executed at OT 1:51, 1:27 and 1:17 with the enemy left tower going 1374 -> 323.

Mother Witch is the pivot card in both directions — the pre-declared Tombstone answer ("he has to be making sure that he's saving either Fireball or like an air unit just to instantly block it every time", 344-348s), a deliberate probe to learn the opponent's hand ("if I Mother Witch like this, more often than not he'll just Mega Minion on top of it, which is fine by me", 358-362s), and the counter-push engine he is willing to eat tower damage for at clock 0:08 ("getting this counter push is a little bit more important cuz we need to win the game right here, right now, or we are dead", 456-459s).

Defence is cheap and layered rather than a single big body: Berserker/Minions in front, Fireball on the push, Heal Spirit played pre-emptively against expected ability or Evo Zap damage ("We have to Heal Spirit preemptively cuz I feel like he's going to go for a ability", 443-446s; "in case he has an Evo Zap, I need a Heal Spirit as well", 487-489s). Against the Lava Hound + Balloon push at clock 0:21-0:03 he spends five cheap cards, concedes ~2600 tower HP on purpose, and banks the Cursed Hog counter-push into overtime.

new_deck.rationale: 3.25 average elixir with every win-condition placement in this game made at or over the bridge (Rune Giant (3, 15), Berserker (3, 15), Elite Barbarians (14, 15) and left lane), the single back-line Rune Giant explicitly treated as a conditional exception, and Zap/Fireball cycled onto the tower for chip.
new_deck.why_it_works_md: The Rune Giant is a 4-elixir tank, which lets this list run bridge pressure at a 3.25 average cost instead of the usual beatdown pacing — she can be thrown at the bridge repeatedly rather than saved for one big push, and her enchant multiplies the fast-hitting Berserker and the Minions standing next to her. Elite Barbarians (evolved) supply the punish when the opponent's ground answer is out of cycle, and Ryley plays them off card-counting rather than elixir advantage: "Wait, hold on. He has no ground cards. Let's just E-Barbs at the bridge" (390-391s). Mother Witch is the deck's spell-bait and its answer to spawner buildings — she forces out a Fireball or an air unit every time, and her Cursed Hogs turn a lost defence into a counter-push. Zap and Fireball do the rest: he opens every game by Zapping the tower for free chip and to start the evolution cycle, and in overtime he can close a tower purely by cycling spells ("we just need two Zaps and a Fireball just to finish off this game", 492s). The weakness the match shows is air defence — with only Minions and spells for a Lava Hound plus Balloon push he has to trade tower HP for tempo.
